source.title: Maximal Initial Learning Rates in Deep ReLU Networks
source.authors: Gaurav M. Iyer; Boris Hanin; D. Rolnick

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures sharpness during training under fixed learning rates and reports whether it approaches the edge-of-stability threshold, testing a part of V5 with a different focus and setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports maximal initial learning rates and initialization-dependent sharpness, but those results do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions. Figure 5 is the relevant result for V5. Its learning-rate curves are figure-only; the text describes the trend but does not provide plotted values.
record.test_reason: Figure 5 explicitly replicates Cohen et al. (2021)'s architecture and full-batch sharpness experiment on a 5k CIFAR-10 subset, adding a Kaiming initialization comparison. It tests V5's edge-of-stability component.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 4.3, including the authors' claimed counterexample, but omits the paper's main conclusion: maximal initial learning rate follows empirical power relationships with architecture and initial sharpness under sufficiently large width/depth and a reduced input-layer learning rate. The authors also prove architecture-dependent sharpness bounds. Their claimed counterexample concerns a necessity condition for decreasing sharpness, not V5's statement about divergence below the threshold.
record.recipe_differences: The authors say they replicate Cohen et al. (2021)'s experimental setup, using the same network architecture and a 5k CIFAR-10 subset, while comparing LeCun and Kaiming initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization changes the sharpness trajectory: Kaiming sharpness is larger at initialization and drops steeply early in training; LeCun sharpness behaves differently.

fits_no_version.finding: The maximal initial learning rate scales with architecture and exceeds 2/λ1 at initialization in the reported Kaiming experiments, while guaranteeing only a validation-accuracy threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep ReLU networks can achieve useful early validation accuracy above the initial Hessian-based stability threshold; this threshold learning rate has architecture-dependent scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: R8 shows decreasing sharpness when the learning rate starts below 2/λ1. The authors present this as contradicting a necessity condition attributed to Gilmer et al.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An above-threshold learning rate is not necessary for sharpness to decrease early in training.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), 2023 proceedings (PMLR 202)
record.problems: Figure 5 provides no numeric curve values in the text, and the network size is not stated in the supplied description. The experiment uses a 5k CIFAR-10 subset and reports no control condition for this comparison.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels, and the specified exceptions.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with convolutional depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified alternative initialization recipes.
Learning speed and trainable depth from activation-matched or orthogonal initialization. Initialization-dependent Hessian sharpness alone does not establish these outcomes.

The squared-loss catapult sequence, including a transient loss rise followed by low training loss and divergence at larger rates; divergence despite starting below the stability threshold; and continued loss decline during threshold hovering. Figure 5 reports sharpness and a 99% training-accuracy endpoint, without a training-loss trajectory.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Verdicts use the supplied textual descriptions; the extracted figure text does not permit independent verification of individual curve coordinates. The initialization-sharpness results and maximal-initial-learning-rate experiments do not directly test V4 or the full catapult mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report near-zero training classification error for the convolutional benchmark settings, random or corrupted labels, or regularized recipes named in V1.
Two-layer teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width are not tested.
The paper does not compare plain and residual networks for training error as depth increases, or test the special initialization and normalization-free recipes named in V3.
Although the paper compares initialization schemes, it does not test the activation-matched initialization and trainable-depth claims in V4.
The paper does not test the above-initial-stability catapult mechanism with squared loss in wide networks, nor the claim that some runs diverge despite starting below the threshold.
Batch normalization speed, accuracy, and learning-rate tolerance are not tested.
